chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Say: O Allah, I ask You for conviction for myself, and forgiveness, and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, You are my trust, and You are my hope, and You are my support, and You are my helper. With You I disembark and with You I travel.

He (peace be upon him) said: And whoever goes out on a journey alone, let him say: 'Whatever Allah wills, there is no strength except by Allah. O Allah, comfort my loneliness, and help me in my solitude, and complete my absence (from home).'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for a Muslim traveling alone?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on supplications in the road, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual mindfulness with daily activities, particularly travel. It underscores the concept of *tawakkul* (reliance on Allah) by invoking Him as the ultimate source of strength and comfort, while also addressing the psychological aspect of solitude through specific invocations for those journeying alone. This practice reflects the broader tradition of transforming mundane actions into acts of worship through mindful remembrance (*dhikr*).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Isa Bin Abdullah Al qummi, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the conviction for myself, and the Forgiveness, and the good health in the world and the Hereafter. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are my Reliable One, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my Hope, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my backbone, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my Helper. With You<sup>azwj</sup> I disembark and with You<sup>azwj</sup> do I travel’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who goes out alone in a journey, so let him say, ‘Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires. There is no Strength except by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Comfort me in my fear, and Support me upon my loneliness, and End my absence (from home)’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Qummiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that you should say, ‘O Allah, I appeal before You to grant my soul certainty, forgiveness and good health in this life and in the next life. O Allah, You are my trustee, my hope, my shoulder (power) and my supporter. With Your help I disembark and travel.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If one travels alone he should say, ‘Whatever Allah wills happens. There is no power without the help of Allah. O Allah, comfort me in my fear, help me in my loneliness and make the end of my absence (from my home) closer.’”
